full_judgment:
Farah Mahbub J : Since the issues as have been posed are common in all these four Writ Petitions hence, the same are being disposed of by this single judgment.

2. In Writ Petition No. 6611 of 2004 the petitioners have challenged the appointment of Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Chittagong, namely Mr Md Abdur Rouf, being violative of Article 116 of the Constitution and section 4(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and also the order No. 9 dated 29-6-03 passed by the Adalat if Mortgage Execution Case No. 35 of2002 transferring the same under the Ain, 2003 and renumbered as Artha Execution Case No. 693.of 2003.

3. Short facts, as are necessary for the purpose of disposal of this Rule, we that the respondent No. 3, Janata Bank, Laldighi Purbapar Branch, Chittagong as plaintiff instituted Mortgage Suit No. 57 of 1996 impleading the petitioners as defendant Nos. 1 and 2 for a claim of Taka 49,79,194.32. Having received the summons of the said suit the defendants-petitioners appeared and contested the same by filing written statement. Upon the consideration of evidence, both oral and documentary, the Adalat decreed the suit on 13-7-01 on contest against the defendants-petitioners for an amount of Taka 49,79,194.32 with interest @ 18% per annum till realisation. The petitioners having defaulted in repaying the decretal amount within the prescribed time the decree holder-Bank . initiated Execution Case No. 35 of 2002 on 13-6-02 Meanwhile, the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter referred as the said Ain) came into operation and in view of section 60(3) of the said Ain the said Execution Case was shown transferred by the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 15t Court, Chittagong to the same Court on 29-6-03 and was renumbered as Arrha Rin Execution Case No. 693 of 2003.

4. Challenging the said impugned order of transfer dated 29-6-03 along with the appointment of the respective Judge of the Adalat the petitioners have preferred the instant application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule.

5. In Writ Petition No. 6612 of 2004 the petitioners have challenged the appointment of judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Chittagong, namely Mr Md Abdur Rouf Sheikh, being violative of Article 116 of the Constitution and section 4(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 along with the order No. 9 dated 9-6-03 passed by the Adalat in Money Execution Case No. 26 of 2002 transferring the same under Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and renumbered as Artha Execution Case No 497 of 2003 and also the order No. 18 dated 22-6-2004 passed by the Adalat issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioners under section 34(1) of the Ain, 2003.

6. The facts of the case, are that the respondent No.3, Janata Bank, Laldighir Purbapar branch, Chittagong instituted Money Suit No. 46 of 1996 impleading the petitioners as defendant Nos. 1 and 2 for a claim of Taka 59,66,821. The petitioners appeared and contested the suit by filing written statement. Subsequently, the Adalat upon considering all the material evidence, both oral as well as documentary, decreed the suit on contest against the defendants-petitioners on 31-7-07. Due to failure of the defendants to pay off the decretal amount within the prescribed period of time the decree-holder Bank initiated Money Execution Case No. 26 of 2002. Meanwhile, due to promulgation of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the money execution case was shown transferred under section 60(3) of the Ain by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Chittagong to the same Court vide order dated 9-6-03. Later, the service of notice under Order XXI, rule 30 of the Code of Civil Procedure (hereinafter referred to as the Code) having not been returned even after a lapse of more than one year from the date of issuance of the same the Adalat issued warrant of arrest on 22-6-04 against the petitioners under section 34(1) of the Ain upon allowing the prayer of the decree holder-Bank. Challenging the orders dated 9-6-03 and 22-6-04 respectively along with the appointment of the judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, the petitioner has preferred the instant application and obtained the present Rule under Article 102 of the Constitution.

7. In Writ Petition No. 6732 of 2004, the petitioner has challenged the appointment of the judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court, Dhaka namely Mr Syed Zahed Mansur, being violative of Article 116 of the Constitution and section 4(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and also the order Nos. 64 and 64A dated 8-1-04 passed by the Adalat in Title Execution Case No. 19 of 1998 restoring the same upon allowing the application under section 33(5) of the Ain, 2003.

8. The facts of the case, in short, are that the respondent No.3, Al Baraka Bank Bangladesh Limited, Islampur Branch, Dhaka (now the Oriental Bank) instituted Title Suit No. 64 of 1995 before the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court, Dhaka on 16-5-95 impleading three defendants including the petitioner as defendant No. 2 for a claim of Taka 8,41,136. The petitioner appeared and contested the suit by filing written statement. After considering the evidence, both oral and documentary, the Adalat passed a compromise decree on 10-3-97. The petitioner having defaulted in complying with the terms of the said compromise decree the decree-holder Bank -initiated Decree Execution Case No. 19 of. 1998 on 23-3-98 for realisation of the decretal amount upon selling the mortgage property mentioned in the schedule of the decree. During continuation of the execution case, at one point it was dismissed by the Adalat on 2-3-03 for not taking steps by the decree holder-Bank. Subsequently, by filing an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 3-2-03 the decree holder-Bank prayed for setting aside the order of dismissal. The said Bank again by filing a separate application on 8-7-03 sought for issuance of certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain. Vide order dated 8-7-03 the Adalat rejected both the applications filed on 3-2-03 and 8-7-03 respectively. Again, on 7-8-03 the decree holder-Bank sought for restoration of the execution proceeding which was rejected by the Adalat vide order dated 21-9-03 Later, on a fresh application filed by the said Bank on 8-1-04, the Adalat upon setting aside the earlier order dated 21-9-03 restored the execution case to its original file and number and on the same date the Adalat also issued certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain. Accordingly, vide order dated 12-7-04 the execution case was disposed of.

9. Challenging the impugned order of restoration vide order Nos. 64 and 64a along with appointment of judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court, Dhaka, the petitioner preferred the instant application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule.

10. In Writ Petition No. 5347 of 2004 the petitioner has challenged the appointment of judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Dhaka namely Mr Md Mozammel Haque being violative of Article 116 of the Constitution under section 4(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and also impugned the proceedings of Artha Execution Case No. 104 of 1999 arising out of Title Suit No. 149 of 1995.

11. Short facts of the case are that the respondent No.3, Janata Bank, Mouchak Branch, Ramna, Dhaka instituted Title Suit No. 149 of 2005 before the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Commercial Court and Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka impleading three defendants including the petitioner as defendant No.2 for a claim of Taka 14,98,041. Ultimately, the suit was decreed ex parte against all the defendants including the petitioner on 14-1-1999. Subsequently, the defendants having not satisfied the decretal amount within the prescribed time the decree holder-Bank started Decree Execution Case No. 104 of 1999 on 19-8-99. While the proceeding was pending for auction sale of the mortgage property the petitioner by filing an application on 24-3-04 sought for staying further proceeding of the execution case, which was rejected by the Adalat vide order dated 9-4-04.

12. Challenging the entire proceeding of the execution case the petitioner preferred the instant application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule.

13. So far the appointments of the judges of the respective Adalat are concerned Mr Munir Sharif, the learned Advocate for the petitioners in all these four Rules, submits that he will not press the portion of the Rule in view of the decisions so given by the apex Court as well as by this bench of the High Court Division.

14. However, the main contentions of Mr Shah Md Munir Sharif, the learned Advocate for the petitioners in all those four Writ Petitions are that the words "বিচারাধীন মামলা” as are found in section 60(3) of the Ain are only relating to the transfer of "suit" which is pending "under trial" under the Ain, 1990, not any other proceedings arising out of the said suit. In this regard, the learned Advocate submits that the impugned execution proceeding being neither "মামলা” nor "বিচারাধীন " the order of transfer of the same by the Adalat under section 60(3) of the Ain is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. In order to substantiate his argument, the learned Advocate further contends that the word "মামলা" used in section 60(3) of the Ain has been issued not in a generic or vagrant sense so as to include any and every kind of action pending in a Court of law. Rather, it has been referred to the usual and accepted sense which is known as "suit". As such, the instant execution proceeding is a continuous wrong which is liable to be declared to have been proceeded with without lawful authority. In support of the said view, the learned Advocate has referred the case of House Building Finance Corporation vs Jahanara Akhter reported in 49 DLR (AD) 80.

15. Mr Sharif, on placing section 6 of the General Clauses Act, next submits that when a statute in followed by a fresh enactment on the subject the consequences of section 6 of the Act will follow unless a contrary intention appears in the new enactment. In the present case, he submits, the statute, the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, does not confer any different intention so as to include an execution proceeding to proceed under the Ain, 2003 by virtue of its section 60(3). Hence, the impugned proceeding is being proceeded with without lawful authority and is liable to be struck down.

16. In addition to the submissions made so far "বিচারাধীন মামলা”  is concerned, Mr Sharif further submits that the impugned order dated 22-6-04 passed by the Adalat under section 34(1) of the Ain in connection with Writ Petition No. 6612 of 2004 is without lawful authority as because on the face of the record it appears that the execution proceeding though initiated under the Ain, 1990 but after promulgation of the new Ain, 2003 the said proceeding having been allegedly brought within the periphery of the Ain, 2003 the Adalat before invoking section 34 of the Ain, 2003 ought to have first issued notice under section 30 of the Ain and also was required to comply with the provisions as constrained in section 33 of the said Ain. For not having done so the said impugned order is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is without any legal effect. Mr Sharif, lastly, contends that the impugned order Nos. 64 and 64a dated 8-1-04 passed by the Adalat in Writ Petition No. 6732 of 2004, whereby the Adalat has restored the execution proceeding upon setting aside its earlier order of dismissal and also in the same breath issued certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain is contrary to the provision so laid down in section 28(3) of the Ain for not exhausting the procedures as provided under section 33(1) (2) (3) and (4) of the A in and, as such, is without jurisdiction, for the legislature did not give mandate to the Adalat to skip the provision as contained in sections 30 and 33(1)-(4) in order to issue certificate under section 33(5) of the said Ain. Hence, the impugned execution proceeding is liable to be declared to have been proceeded with without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

17. Conversely, Mr Md Akbar Ameen Babul, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent-Bank in Writ Petition Nos. 6611 of 2004 and 6612 of 2004 by filing affidavit-in-opposition submits that on a plain reading of the entire provisions as contained in Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 it will be apparent that the legislature has intentionally used the word "মামলা”  in its generic term so as to include its "execution proceeding". Because to cover up the transitional period for those suits as well the execution proceeding lying pending for disposal before the Artha Rin Adalat established or declared under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 the legislature has expressly incorporated section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003 with words "স্থানান্তরিত হইবে" means transfer by operation of law, not to any other Adalat or Court of law but in the same Adalat which has been newly established and/or declared as Artha Rin Adalat under the Ain, 2003 on the repeal of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990.

18. Refuting the contention of the petitioner that "execution proceeding" is not a "বিচারাধীন মামলা" to be transferred under the Ain, 2003 the learned Advocate for the respondent Bank submits that the general meaning of the word "বিচারাধীন মামলা" though may be taken as "suits pending for adjudication" but it may also be meant as "pending under judicial consideration". In this regard, he further submits that the execution proceeding, no doubt, is a part of the suit pending before a court of law to give effect to the decree passed against the judgment debtors. In consequence, it definitely is inclusive of "বিচারাধীন মামলা". As because even if, for argument's sake, it is agreed that execution proceeding is not a "বিচারাধীন মামলা" to be transferred under the Ain, 2003 then, in consequence, all the decrees awaiting its execution in a proceeding initiated under Order XXI of the Code shall hang in the air, which cannot be the intention of the legislature while promulgating the Ain, 2003. The learned Advocate, lastly, submits that the petitioners have admittedly contested the suit and accordingly, respective decrees have been passed in both the suits. Moreover, in both the cases the decrees were not satisfied by the petitioners within the prescribed time fixed by the Adalat. Ultimately, in order to realise the same Execution Case No. 35 of 2002 in Writ Petition No. 6611 of 2004 started and continued for more than 2 years but could not reach. its finality. Whereas, in Execution Case No. 26 of 2002 in Writ Petition No. 6612 of 2004 a notice issued under Order XXI, rule 30 of the Code having not been returned even after a lapse of 1 year and 4 months, the Adalat had to issue warrant of arrest under section 34(1) of the Ain in order to realise the decretal amount with a view to create pressure upon, the judgment debtors-petitioners to pay off the decretal dues. But all these efforts have become futile with the stay of the further proceedings of the said case on 4-12-04 without even challenging the judgment and decree. Accordingly, the learned Advocate submits that the petitioners having failed to substantiate any of the grounds so taken in those Writ Petitions the Rule should be discharged with costs.

19. Mr Masud Ahmed Sayeed, the learned Advocate appearing in Writ Petition No. 5347 of 2004, on behalf of the respondent No.3, Janata Bank and Mr Md Monowar Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing in Writ Petition No. 6732 of 2004 on behalf of the respondent No. 3, Al Baraka Bank Ltd (now the Oriental Bank Ltd), submit that they have nothing to add further on the point of law so advanced by the learned Advocate for the respondent-Bank in other two Writ Petitions.

20. However, the Government has filed power in all the writ petitions but they did not come for- ward with any affidavit-in-opposition nor made any substantive submissions on any of the points so raised in these Rules. Whereas office of the learned Attorney-General is supposed to render assistance particularly when vires of any statutory provision has been put under challenge. Such attitude of the learned law officers of the Attorney-General Office is highly deprecated.

21. Heard the learned Advocates of all the contending parties, perused the writ petitions along with the impugned orders and the affidavit-in-oppositions filed by the respective respondents in all these four Writ petitions. The common question being posed by the respective petitioners is, that whether the "execution proceeding" lying pending to execute the decree can be identified as "মামলা" and if so, whether it is a "বিচারাধীন মামলা" which can be transferred by the respective Adalat in order to bring the same within the periphery of section 60(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003.

22. However, in order to appreciate the respective arguments so advanced by the learned Advocates of the contending parties, let us first consider the Preamble and section 60(1) and (3) of the Ain which provide thus:

"আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক ঋণ আদায়ের জন্য প্রচলিত আইনের অধিকতর সংশোধন ও সংহতকরণকল্পে প্রণীত আইন।”

“৬০(১) অর্থ ঋণ আদালত আইন, ১৯৯০ (১৯৯০) সালের ৪নং আইন) এতদ্বারা রহিত করা হইল।

(২) ..........................................................................................

(৩) অর্থ ঋণ আদালত আইন, ১৯৯০ এর রহিতকরণ সত্ত্বেও, উক্ত রহিত আইনের অধীনে অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে বিচারাধীন সকল মামলা অত্র আইনের অধীনে প্রতিষ্ঠিত বা ঘোষিত অনুরূপ আদালতে বিচারাধীন মামলা হিসাবে বদলী হইবে এবং উহারা পূর্বের আদালতে যে পর্যায়ে বিচারাধীন ছিল সেই পর্যায় হইতে বিচারধীন থাকিবে এবং ঐ সকল মামলার ক্ষেত্রে এই আইনের বিধানাবলী, যতদূর সম্ভব, এমনভাবে প্রযোজ্য হইবে, যেন উক্ত মামলাসমূহ এই আইনের অধীনেই দায়ের হইয়াছিল।”

<u>23. On a plain reading of the preamble of the statute, it transpires that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (Act VIII of 2003) was promulgated with a view to further consolidate and amend the existing law i.e. Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 for speedy recovery of loan of the financial institution. Whereas, by virtue of section 60(1) of the Ain, 2003 the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 has altogether been repealed and in explicit terms the legislature manifested its clear intention in section 60(3) that so far pending cases are concerned the provision enunciated under Ain, 2003, are to be made applicable. In other words, the Ain, 2003 did not conceive any saving clause in order to make the earlier repealed Ain applicable for the pending cases to be disposed of under the Ain, 1990.</u>

24. Now, the Ain 2003, particularly in section 60(3), the legislature incorporated the ড়িৎফং উক্ত রহিত আইনের অধীনে অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে বিচারাধীন সকল মামলা অত্র আইনের অধীনে প্রতিষ্ঠিত বা ঘোষিত অনুরূপ আদালতে বিচারাধীন মামলা হিসাবে বদলী হইবে।"

25. However, after promulgation of the Ain, 2003 no English text of the said Ain has yet been published. Hence, in order to have a clear perspective of the words used by the legislature in section 60(3) the dictionary meaning of the same may be resorted to although those meanings are not to be taken as authoritative exponents of the meaning of the words used in the statute.

26. In the আইন শব্দ কোষ” compiled and edited by Mr Justice Muhammad Habibur Rahman and Mr Anisuzzaman, published by "Anyaprokash, Dhaka the word ' মামলা” has been identified as "case, cause, litigation; suit; whereas, the word '“বিচারাধীন মামলা” has been quoted to mean "pending action, lis pendens". Therefore, the বাংলা” portion of the provision quoted above may be translated as "all litigations pending in the Adalat under the repealed Ain, the Ain, 1990, shall be transferred to the Adalat established or declared under the Ain, 2003 as pending cause or litigation."

<u>27. We, however, know that the statute is to be construed according "to the intent of them that make it" and the duty of judicature is to act upon the true intention of the Legislature-the "Mens or sentensia legis." The Courts have, therefore, to look essentially to the words of the statute to discern the "referent" aiding their effort as much as possible by the context. The context here means, the statute as a whole, the previous state of the law, other statutes in pari materia, the general scope of the statute and the mischief that it was intended to remedy, as has been mandated by the Supreme Court of India in the case of Union of India vs Elphinstone Spinning and Weaving Co. Ltd, 2001 (1) JT SC, P 563. In this regard, the observations made by Lord Davey in Canada Sugar Refining Company vs R(l898) AC 735, P 742 is apt to be quoted as "Every clause of a statute should be construed with reference to the con- text and other clauses of the Act, so as, as far as possible, to make a consistent enactment of the whole statute or series of statutes relating to the subject matter." It is spoken of construction "ex-visceribus actus". However, it is also a golden rule of construction that the words of a statute, when there is doubt about their meaning, are to be understood in the sense in which they best harmonise with the subject of the enactment and the object which the Legislature has in view. Their meaning is found not so much in a strict grammatical or etymological property of language, nor even in its popular use, as in the subject or on the occasion in which they are used, and the object to be attained.</u>

28. Now, the proposition being posed by the petitioner is that, the impugned "execution proceeding" is neither a "মামলা" for the word "মামলা " only signifies a "suit" which involves adjudication of the issues so claimed by the contending parties, nor it qualifies to be a "বিচারাধীন মামলা” as because at the stage of execution proceeding nothing remains for determination of any further dispute except to execute its own decree.

29. The word "execution" has been termed in Wharton's Law Lexicon, 14th Edition, at page 387 as "the last state of a suit whereby possession is obtained of anything recovered by a judgment; which is also styled as final process of the suit:". In P Ramanatha Aiyer's Law Lexicon the word "execution" has been provided as "when there still remains something substantial to be done under a decree before it can become thoroughly effectual, that decree has to be executed within the meaning of the Code of Civil Procedure." In Mahmudul Islam's Law of Civil Procedure the "execution of a decree" has been termed as the "enforcement by the process of the Court of its own decrees or orders following the procedural details and the mode of execution provided in the statute." In other words, upon obtaining a judgment and decree passed by a court of law on proving its claim in accordance with law accrues a substantive right in favour of the decree holder-bank or financial institution to have the decree executed through the process of law. Therefore, "execution proceeding" is a form of process mandated by a statute wherein the Adalat, on the prayer of the decree holder bank, authorises to sell so much of the judgment debtor's non-exempt property as is necessary to satisfy the decree and render it complete with the consequence that nothing remains to be done to make it a complete and effective decree.

30. By the "Remedial statute", the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (Act VIII of 2003) the legislature has repealed the Ain, 1990 in its entirety and incorporated a separate chapter, namely Chapter VI, under the heading " জারী ", providing procedures to be adopted by the decree holder-Bank for dealing with execution process starting from sections 26-39. Now, on a close examination of these provisions of law, particularly section 27(2), it appears that the legislature has incorporated জারীর মামলাটি কার্যকর করার জন্য * * * * |"  Moreso, under section 28(1), for execution of decree, ডিক্রীদার, ধারা ২৯ এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, জারীর জন্য আদালতে দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিয়া মামলা করিবে।: Also, under section 28(2) says উপ-ধারা (১)-এর বিধানে ব্যত্যয়ে, * * * জারীর জন্য দায়েরকৃত কোন মামলা তামাদিতে বারিত হইবে * * *"; sub-section (3) provides: জারীর জন্য দ্বিতীয় বা পরবর্তী মামলা, প্রথম বা পূর্ববর্তী জারীর মামলা খারিজ বা নিষ্পত্তি হওয়ার পরবর্তী এক বৎসর সময় উত্তীর্ণ হওয়ার পরে দাখিল করা হইলে,* * * * * * |" sub-section (4) says, জারীর জন্য কোন নতুন মামলা প্রথম জারীর * 	* ।"

31. From the above quoted relevant provisions of law it can clearly be discerned that the legislature while enacting this piece of legislation has made "execution proceeding" inclusive of মামলা” This view of ours is further fortified on reading section 5(1) of the Ain, which states, ঋণ আদায় সম্পর্র্কিত যাবতীয় মামলা * * * । Further section 4(3) provides জারীর উপ-ধারা (১) বা (২) এর অধীন কোন অর্থ ঋণ আদালত প্রতিষ্ঠিত বা ঘোষিত না হইয়া থাকিলে,  আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের ঋণ আদায় সম্পর্কিত মামলা সংশ্লিষ্ট অধিক্ষেত্রের যুগ্ম-জেলা জজ আদালতে দায়ের করিতে হইবে; এবং এই আইনের বিধানাবলী ঐ সকল মামলা শুনানী, জারী, আপীল ইত্যাদি যাবতীয় কার্যক্রমে এমনভাবে অনুসরণীয় হইবে, যেন উক্ত যুগ্ম জেলা-জজ আদালত এই আইনের প্রতিষ্ঠিত বা ঘোষিত আদালত এবং এই আইনের উদ্দেশ্য সাধন কল্পে উক্ত যুগ্ম জেলা জজের আদালত এই আইনের অধীন অর্থ ঋণ আদালত হিসাবে গণ্য হইবে।” and sub-section 4 says বিচারাধীন অন্য সকল মামলা তাঁহার এখতিয়ারাধীন অন্য কোন যুগ্ম-জেলা জজ আদালতে বদলীর নিদের্শ দান করিবেন।"

32. Moreso, section 60(3) of the Ain, on the face of it, concerns with the transitional period of formation or constitution of new Artha Rin Adalat under the subsequent enactment for using the words, "বদলী হইবে”, necessitating transfer of suit, file and all pending proceedings, by operation of the newly enacted law. In other words, the intention of the Parliament, as evident from the language used in section 60(3), is to be effected by the administrative action of the Adalat itself, to accommodate the change pursuant to introduction of the new Ain.

33. Now, the Adalat, created under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 where in "মামলা” was initiated, had the power to execute the respective decree by entertaining execution case under section 6Ka of the Ain, 1990. Upon repeal of the Ain, 1990 the respective Adalats created thereunder have also been abolished. In consequence, all the cases relating to recovery of loan pending in those Adalats stood transferred under section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003 to the Artha Rin Adalat created under the new Ain, 2003 giving statutory power to dispose of all the pending cases in accordance with the provisions of the Ain, 2003, as far as possible.

34. However, the petitioner has contended that the apex Court in the case of House Building Finance Corporation vs Jahanara Akhter reported in 49 DLR (AD) 80 observed that "the action contemplated under Article 27 of President's Order 27 of 1973 is outside the concept of মামলা” which correspond only with the suit under section 5(1) of the Ain, 1990". On examining the said decision it appears that originally House Building Finance Corporation (HBFC) as "applicant" filed an application under Article 27 as "Miscellaneous case" upon submitting Taka 5 as Court fee for realisation of loan before the learned District Judge, a forum created by the statute, PO 27 of 1973. After promulgation of the Ain, 1990 those "Miscellaneous Applications" terming as "proceeding" were transferred to the Adalat established under the Ain, 1990. Challenging the order of transfer, the petitioner of the said writ petition preferred application before the learned District Judge which was rejected by the Court. Against which writ petition was filed and the Rule was made absolute by the High Court Division. While deciding the point whether proceeding initiated under President's Order 27 of 1973 can be equated with the "suit" the apex Court observed in para 14 which runs thus:

"An application under Article 27 cannot be equated with the suit, for in an application under that Article none of the requirements as in a suit is attracted. No plaint, no Court fee, no limitation, no written statement, no other necessary steps, no decree, nothing. The financial institution is to get relief or reliefs in a summary manner which is not available in the, form of a suit."

35. We are also in full agreement with the said view that the application heading as "Miscellaneous proceeding" initiated under the President's Order No. 27 of 1973 filed for realisation of loan does not squarely fulfil the criterion of a suit. But that cannot give inference that proceeding initiated under section 27 of the Ain, 2003 for execution of a decree is not a "মামলা” so far the term “মামলা” is concerned hence, the same is not a "বিচারাধীন মামলা” As because an execution proceeding, first of all, is not a separate or independent case started with adjudication of the claim of any bank or financial institution. Rather, claim of the plaintiff-bank having been proved resulted in a judgment and decree. In consequence, the decree holder accrued a substantive right in his favour to have the decree executed through process of law under an execution proceeding. Hence, the facts and circumstances of the Jahanara Akhter's Case being altogether different cannot be applicable in the present case. Moreover, even the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank having its own statute used the term "miscellaneous proceeding" initiated against the defaulted borrower, and has given special power to the District Judge to dispose of those proceedings where payment of Taka 5 as Court fee is to be submitted for entertaining such "Miscellaneous proceeding". Moreso, under the first proviso to section 5 of the Ain, 1990 and section 5(6) of the Ain, 2003 the financial institutions have dual capacity, either by filing a regular suit before the Artha Rin Adalat where ad valorem Court fee is to be payable or before the District Judge by filing a "Miscellaneous proceeding" on payment of Taka 5 as Court fee and in both the forums same relief can be prayed for. In other words, for the same purpose the legislature has given two forums in one occasion known as "Miscellaneous Proceeding" and also the "suits".

<u>36. Whereas, so far the Ain, 2003 is concerned in its generic sense the entire power and function of the predecessor Adalat established under the Ain, 1990 virtually devolved upon the only lone successor Adalat established under the Ain, 2003. Considering the submissions so advanced by the learned Advocates for the petitioner, if we go to exclude all the execution cases from the hand of the present Artha Rin Adalat where all those cases shall go, which is to be looked into vigorously because after the abolition of the Ain, 1990 there is none to share the legacies of that Adalat except its successor, the present Adalat, established under the Ain, 2003. However, the key to the opening of every law is the reason and the spirit of the law it is the animus imponentis, the intention of the law maker, expressed in the law itself, taken as a whole. Hence, to arrive at the true meaning of any particular phrase in a statute, that particular phrase is not to be viewed detached from the context.</u>

37. Section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003 clearly projects the view that the Adalats declared and/or established under section 4(5) of the Ain, 2003 has entirely inherited, and has been empowered to succeed the Adalat established under the Ain, 1990. In the present context, the "execution proceeding" initiated under section 27 of the Ain, following the procedures as enumerated in sections 30 and 33 of the Ain and the Code of Civil Procedure, so far the same are not inconsistent with it, can well be construed and designated as part of the suit, awaiting disposal of the decree in its final process for obtaining the possession of property, moveable or immovable, acquired by judgment of law. In the case of Rahe Manjil Transport vs Md Amin reported in PLD 1963, Karachi (DB) 182 it was held, "if the proceedings in which the judgment is given are in the nature of suit it is quite apparent that the execution proceeding are also a part of such 'suit ..... ........ " In other words, it is a necessary part of the suit which gives finality to the adjudication in the suit upon satisfying the claim of the decree holder-Bank.

38. Keeping in of the said observation, the words বিচারাধীন মামলা” as appears in section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003 shall have to be interpreted in more wider sense than that of the Jahanara Akther's Case reported in 49 DLR (AD) 80. Because in that case there were more than one forum created by the statute itself to obtain and execute its own decree. Here, the legislature had a clear intention to make over all the cases pending before the Adalat established under the Ain, 1990 being abolished and since no other alternative is found to have been created by the legislature certainly all the "suits", "cases" or "execution proceeding" whatever might be which are liable to be disposed of by the Adalat under the Ain, 1990 shall come within the ambit of the present statute, the Ain, 2003 and to be disposed of by the lone successor, the Adalat established under the Ain, 2003, since it is a "Remedial Statute."

39. Be that as it may, having due regard to the observations and findings made hereinabove, we are of the view that in exercise of power under section 60(3) the Adalat declared and/or established under the Ain, 2003 with lawful mandate transferred the "Execution Cases" which were lying pending for disposal under the repealed Ain, 1990 before the Adalat which has also been abolished with the promulgation of the Ain, 2003 in order to give finality to the decree. Accordingly, so far the question of transfer of "execution proceeding" under section 60(3) of the Ain is concerned, the respective Rules in all the four Writ Petitions do not have any merit, and accordingly, are liable to be discharged.

40. However, in Writ Petition No. 6612 of 2004 the petitioner has also challenged the order dated 22-6-04, issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioners. However, it appears from the record that the respective execution proceedings were initiated under the repealed Ain, the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. But during its proceeding the new Ain, the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, came into force. Accordingly, as per section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003 all pending execution proceedings shown transferred under the new Ain with the enforcement of all the provisions contained therein. However, in this regard, it is the emphatic contention of the learned Advocate that the Adalat after having transferred the execution proceeding under section 60(3) of the Ain neither issued notice under section 30 nor complied with the procedures as contained in section 33 of the Ain. Accordingly, the Adalat is debarred from issuing any warrant of arrest on the application of the decree holder-bank under section 34(I) of the Ain. The said contention also finds it stand from the record wherefrom it is apparent that no notice under section 30 of the Ain was ever issued by the respective Adalat. If that be so, question of issuing warrant of arrest under section 34( 1) does not arise. In view of the said violation of the express provision of law, which was required to be complied with by the Adalat before passing the impugned order dated 22-6-04 under section 34(1) of the Ain, so far the issuance of the warrant of arrest against the petitioner is concerned, is liable to be declared to be without lawful authority.

41. In the result, so far passing of the impugned order dated 22-6-04 by the Adalat in issuing warrant of arrest under section 34( I) of the Ain against the petitioner is concerned, the instant Rule has merit.

42. In Writ Petition No. 6732 of 2004 the further claim of the petitioner is, that the restoration of the execution case being hit by section 28(3) of the Ain, the same is liable to have been passed with- out lawful authority and is of no legal effect. From the record, it appears that admittedly after passing the compromise decree on 10-3-97 application was preferred for execution of the same on 23-3-98 for failure of the petitioner to comply with the terms of compromise Subsequently, it was dismissed by the Adalat vide order dated 2-3-03 for not taking steps by the respondent-bank. On the very next day, i.e. 3-3-03, the respondent-bank preferred application for restoration of the execution case. While the said application was pending the respondent-bank preferred another application on 8-7-03 under section 33(5) of the Ain for issuance of certificate. Both the applications dated 3-3-03 and 8-7-03, respectively, were rejected by the Adalat vide order dated 8-7-03. an 7-8-03, another application was made for restoration which was rejected by the Adalat on 21-9-2003. Subsequently, upon a fresh application by the decree-holder Bank the Adalat restored the Execution Case vide order dated 8-1-2004. Now, as per section I (3) of the Ain, the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into force on 1-5-03. Accordingly, the limitation period for execution proceeding shall commence from 1-5-03. From the record it is apparent that the application for restoration which was filed earlier on 3-3-03 was rejected on 8-7-03 and the Adalat subsequently allowed the application by order dated 8-\-04 which is well within one year as required under section 28(1) of the Ain. Hence, we are of the view that there is no necessity or scope for filing fresh execution case under section 28(3) of the Ain, 2003.

<u>43. However, though we have found that the restoration of the Miscellaneous Execution Case is valid but in order No. 64a i.e. issuance of certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain, which has been passed by the Adalat on 8-1-04 i.e. the day when the execution case was restored to its file and number, cannot be accepted as tenable in the eye of law because after the execution case was transferred under section 60(3) of the Ain the executing Court would proceed from the stage where the execution proceeding was lying pending for disposal. As such, issuance of sale certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain on the same day when execution case was restored without exhausting the procedures as provided under section 33(1), (2), (3) and (4) of the Ain resorting to a short-cut way is not tenable in the eye of law. In that view of the matter, the impugned order dated 8-1-04 so far as issuing certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain in favour of the decree-holder Bank, is illegal and without lawful authority.</u>

44. Accordingly, so far it relates to issuance of certificate under section 33(5) in favour of the decree-holder Bank is concerned, we find substance in the instant Rule.

45. Considering the facts and circumstances and in view of the reasons and discussions made hereinabove, all the four Rules relating- to appointment of Judges of the respective Adalats, and transfer of the respective cases under section 60(3) of the Ain 2003 are discharged. So, far passing of the impugned order dated 22-6-04 under section 34(1) of the Ain, the Rules in Writ Petition No. 6612 of 2004 and issuance of certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain in Writ Petition No. 6732 of 2004 are made absolute.

However, there will be no order as to costs.

End.

parties:
Abdus Sobhan Sheikh ------ Petitioner
vs
Kazi Moulana Jabedullah and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued at the instance of the pre-emptor in a proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act against the judgment and order dated 24-6-96 passed in Misc. Appeal 4 of 1992 by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Bagerhat affirming the judgment and order dated 22-1-92 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1986, by the Senior Assistant Judge Bagerhat disallowing the prayer for pre-emption, of the present petitioner who is admittedly a co-sharer in the case holding.

2. The petitioner filed the Original pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 67 of 1987 on 19-8-85 under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act because the land under pre-emption is a part of the homestead. But the disputed land is situated beyond municipal area. The transfer was completed under section 60 of the Registration Act on 20-6-85. The application for pre-emption was filed within 120 days ie within the period of limitation. The pre-emptee filed written objection contending inter alia, that since the land under pre, emption was not within the municipal area the pre-emption case should have been filed under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, Therefore the pre-emptor came up with an application for amendment of the plaint of the pre-emption case. The amendment application was filed on 4-11-89. That was allowed on 5-11-89 converting the pre-emption case under section 96 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act. According to section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act, the pre-emptor deposited the entire consideration money and 5% compensation on it and accordingly, the present petitioner preemptor deposited an amount of Taka 1250.00 as compensation. The total deposit was Taka 26,250.00 made before filing of the case. After the case was converted under section 960f the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as per amendment, the pre-emptor was required to make deposit of further 5% compensation that is to make the deposit of compensation @ 10% being further Taka 1250.00 as was required under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, The deposit was made on 5-11-89 after the said amendment. Against the said amendment both as to conversion of the case and for depositing the additional compensation the pre-emptee did not raise any objection and did not move higher forum.

3. The ground for pre-emption of the pre-emptor principally is that he is a co-sharer and the purchaser is a stranger and without giving notice under section 89 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the sale was made. The pre-emption case was however filed within time. On contest the trial Court dismissed the pre-emption case on the ground that the case was bad for defect of party finding that one Obaidul Hoque was not made party in the pre-emption proceeding.

4. The pre-emptor took the appeal and the appellate Court on hearing both parties found that the pre-emption case was not bad for non-joinder of any necessary party because that Obaidul Hoque had already transferred his share to one Fazle Ali who again sold the same to one Shaizuddin Ahamed, who has been made opposite party No. 5 in the pre-emption case. But the appellate Court dismissed the appeal on two grounds namely, on limitation for reason that the remaining 5% of the compensation was paid after the statutory period of 120 days and secondly, on the grounds of waiver acquiescence and estoppel, by the impugned judgment and order.

5. Against that the judgment and order of the appellate Court the, pre-emptor has obtained this present Rule.

6. As it is found so far the question of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence is concerned, no issue was framed in the trial Court as no specific allegation was made in the written objection filed by the pre-emptor in the trial Court. In this deposition the DW 1 the pre-emptee has only stated that the pre-emptor was present at the time of execution and registration of the deed of sale in question in the office of the sub-registrar. But this lone statement judgment has not been corroborated by any other witness or evidence.

Section 115 of the Evidence Act reads as follows.

"When one person has, by his declaration, act or omission, intentionally caused or permitted another person to believe a thing to be true and to act upon such belief, neither he nor his representative shall be allowed, in any suit or proceeding between himself and such person or his representative to deny the truth of that thing."

So according to the said definition or constitution of estoppel as there is no other specific allegation or evidence excepting the allegation that the preemptor was present at the time of execution and registration of the deed in question, it cannot be accepted that the pre-emptor could establish or prove the said allegation or any activity against the pre-emptor which could constitute against the pre-emptor the plea of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence.

<u>7. Moreover, right of pre-emption which is a statutory right cannot be given up or taken away or waived by mere allegation that the preemptor was present in the sub-registrar's office at the time of execution and registration of the deed in question which also could not be established in this case by the pre-emptor by reliable cogent or corroborative evidence. In the case of Fazeruddin vs Maizuddin and others 44 DLR (AD) 62 it has been held as follows:</u>

<u>"Statutory right of pre-emption cannot be taken away by mere verbal assurance of the person having such right unless other facts and circumstances clearly make out a case of a acquiescence or waiver".</u>

<u>Another moot question in this case is whether in a pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act if the consideration money and part of the compensation is paid or deposited within the statutory period of the limitation being 120 days and another part of compensation only is deposited later on after statutory period but on amendment of the pre-emption application as stated above the case becomes barred by limitation or not.</u>

<u>8. In the case of Sree Shushil Ranjan Dutra vs Al-haj Moulvi Idris Miah; reported in 42 DLR (AD) 110 wherein the judgment was pronounced by his Lordships Mr Badrul Haider Chowdhury J. In para 11 their Lordships have held as follows:</u>

<u>"Amendment of pleadings under Order 7 rule 17 CPC special limitation prescribed under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the question of limitation may arise in two cases (i) whether the claim to be included was barred on the date of institution of the suit (ii) whether the claim is barred on the date of the prayer for amendment. In this case the amendment will-relate back to the date of the institution of the case".</u>

<u>9. Mr Ashfaqul Islam, the learned Counsel for the pre-emptor petitioner cites another decision. It is in the case of Selina Begum and another vs Mofizul Islam and others, reported in 42 DLR (AD) 77 also wherein the judgment was pronounced by his Lordship Mr Badrul Haider Chowdhury J. That case was also under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the question arose whether the balance of consideration money can be deposited beyond four months. In para 5 of the said decision their Lordships have held' as under:</u>

<u>"The learned Counsel appearing for the appellant canvassed that it was statutory obligation on the part of the pre-emptor to deposit the balance consideration within the period and since he failed to, do, so the prayer was illegally granted. This point has no substance. By opposing respondent's payer for deposit of the balance consideration the appellants were trying to achieve something indirectly namely, frustrating the very pre-emption proceeding, the prayer was rightly granted, High Court Division was correct in taking the view".</u>

<u>10. In the instant case it is found that the pre-emptor at first filed the case under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act and the deposit was made of the consideration money and 5% of the same compensation. After conversion of the case under section 96 of the State' Acquisition find Tenancy Act the defect was detected as to deposit of balance of 5% of the compensation. The balance amount was deposited as per order of the trial Court granting amendment application and as such, deposit can be treated and accepted as valid deposit which was made after the amendment of the pre-emption application and the amendment since relates back to the date of filing of the pre-emption case which was made in time, the case, is not barred by limitation. In the case of Md Mofizuddin Sarker vs Md Abdul Jabbar Akhand, reported in 1 BLD 486 which is a Single Bench decision, it has been held that if the application is made within the period of limitation and the consideration money is also deposited in court within the period of limitation, it shall be deemed that the deposit has been made while making the application for pre-emption under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (XXVIII) of 1951 s 96(3 ) (a) (para 2) So the provision of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, wherein it has been stated that the deposit of the consideration money along with 10% compensation shall accompany the pre-emption, application, in view of the said decision. I find that the time for deposit has been relaxed and extended. So the principle as to deposit is not rigid and it is not mandatory that the entire deposit both the consideration money and compensation should be paid before filing of the case. Moreover, in the instant case the deposit of consideration money along with 5% of the compensation was made in time and it accompanied the petition of pre-emption. Only balance of 5% compensation was deposited after amendment.</u>

<u>11. In the case of Akteruzzaman vs Habilullah 31 DLR (AD) 88 (para 28) it has been held that deposit of entire consideration along with 10% compensation for pre-condition must be deposited when the pre-emption application is filed, in compliance of sub-section 3 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. There is some distinction in that case and the instant case. In that the pre-emptor himself made the proportionate deposit by calculating himself later on he made the deposit of the balance amount as per order of the High Court Division, so prayer for preemption was refused in that case by the Appellate Division on the ground of limitation. But in the instant case entire consideration money along with 5% of compensation was deposited before filing of the pre-emption application under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act and after amendment was allowed for converting the case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the remaining 5% of the compensation was deposited since the order of amendment relating back to the date of filing of the case the instant case does not become barred by limitation as it was filed originally within the statutory period of 120 days.</u>

12. Under the circumstances of this case it is found that the learned Counsel who filed the original pre-emption case being confused because of the fact that the case land comprising part of homestead and as such the original application was filed under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act and later on rectification was made by way of amendment of the plaint of the pre-emption case converting it into under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

<u>13. Moreover, I am of the view that for any mistake of a lawyer or laches of him no litigant should suffer. Here in this case the pre-emptor deposited the entire consideration money and 5% of the compensation being Taka 26250.00 before filing of the original pre-emption case so he could pay the balance amount being Taka 1250.00 only for further @ 5% compensation also. Therefore there is no negligence on the part of the pre-emptor so he should not suffer for the mistake of lawyer concerned.</u>

14. The whole framework of the law of pre-emption both under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act and under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has been made with the purpose and intention to check the infiltrators from outside come within a holding enjoyed by its co-sharers.

15. In this case, admittedly the pre-emptor is a co-sharer and the purchaser is a stranger.

16. For the reasons and discussions made above it is held that the appellate Court, committed illegality in dismissing the pre-emption case on point of limitation and also on point of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence and the trial Court committed illegality in dismissing the case for defect of party which has been rightly and legally corrected by the appellate Court.

17. Therefore, the judgments and orders of the courts below are liable to be set aside and the pre-emption case is to be allowed. Thus the Rule in made absolute the judgment and orders of the courts below are set aside. The pre-emption case is allowed.

No order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
Md Abdul Wahhab Miah J: This Rule nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order being No.43 dated 11-5-99 passed by Mr AM Shahidur Rahman, Special Tribunal No.1, Satkhira in Special Tribunal Case No.348 of 1996 arising out of Satkhira Police Station Case No.16 dated 11-4-96 corresponding to OR Case No. 140/96 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. In the writ petition it has been stated, inter alia, that on 9-4-96 four Bangladeshi citizens namely, Shamsuddin, Shamol, Shamim and Motiul Alam came from India with some goods under Baggage Rules and they after completing immigration checking from immigration checking post produced the goods to the Customs House, Jessore for assessing Customs Duty. VAT and other taxes. But their goods were not released and those were temporarily held up due to the arrival of some higher customs officers from Khulna and those passengers were given receipts against their goods. On 10-4-96 at 5-30 PM the present petitioners namely, Sirajul Islam and Md Aminul Islam came from India with Indian goods under Baggage Rules and they kept their goods in a room of Immigration checkpost of Vomra with their legal passports and when they met with the aforesaid 4(four) businessmen who came from India on 9-4-96. They were informed by them that their (the said four persons) goods had not been released till then as in the meantime BDR personnel came to the spot and seized the aforesaid goods on the basis of false and baseless information. Thereafter on 10-4-96 Naik Md Golam Nabi of 21 Rifles Battalion, Satkhira lodged a first information report with Satkhira Police Station against the petitioners and the said 4(four) persons under section 25(B) of the Special Powers Act 1974 and the said First Information Report gave rise to Satkhira Police Station case No.16 dated 10-4-96 corresponding to OR No. 140/96. The Police after investigation submitted final report being No.80 dated 16-7-96 under section 26(B) of the Special Powers Act 1974 stating that the accused persons brought the seized sarees lawfully from India and the First Information Report was lodged upon wrong information. The learned Magistrate 1st Class Nalishi Adaltat Zone 'Kha' Satkhira after receiving the final report by his order dated 1-8-96 sent the case record to the Special Tribunal No.1, Satkhira who took cognizance in the case by this order dated 18-11-96 on the basis of a Naraji Petition filed by the Informant and the case was registered as Special Tribunal Case No.348 of 96. Against the acceptance of Naraji Petition accused persons namely, Md Shamsuddin Ahmed alias Alauddin, Shyamal Mallick and Md Matiul Alam filed Criminal Miscellaneous case No.3231 of 1997 before this court under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the said Special Tribunal Case. Eventually, a Division Bench of this Court by Judgment and Order dated 27-11-1997 made the Rule absolute in the said Criminal Miscellaneous Case and the proceeding of Special Tribunal Case No.348 of 1996 of the Court of Special Tribunal No.1 Satkhira was quashed. After the disposal of the said Criminal Miscellaneous Case Matiul Alam Bhuiyan, Shamal Mittra, Shamim and Shamsuddin who were accused in the said Special Tribunal case filed a petition before the Special Tribunal No.1 Satkhira to release the goods seized by the customs authority in their favour and the learned Special Tribunal by order No.37 dated 3-3-99 directed the Customs authority to return the goods to the claimants as per their individual statement after realising VAT as per law. After the passing of the said order the petitioners filed an application before the learned Special Tribunal Satkhira to stay the operation of said order No.37 dated 3-3-99 till the ascertainment of ownership of the seized goods and the Special Tribunal by his order No.38 dated 16-3-99 directed the customs authority to take necessary order from the tribunal for releasing the goods after submission of the list of the seized goods by them. Thereafter, the present petitioners filed another application before the Special Tribunal No.1 Satkhira for releasing the seized goods in their favour as per the final report submitted by the investigating officer and the Special Tribunal by his order No.42 dated 6-5-99 rejected the petition of the petitioners and maintained the order dated 3-3-99. The petitioners filed a review petition before the Special Tribunal No.1 Satkhira for re-considering the order dated 6-5-99 and the Special Tribunal by his order No.43 dated 11-5-99 maintained the earlier order passed on 3-3-99 and directed the customs authority to return the seized goods to all the 6(six) first information report named accused persons on strict scrutiny of the individual claims. Thereafter the petitioners filed an application before the Special Tribunal Satkhira for staying the operation of order Nos.37 and 43 dated 3-3-99 and dated 11-5-99 respectively who by order No. 44 dated 27-5-99 stayed the operation of the aforesaid orders up to 30-6-99. The petitioners applied for the certified copy of the order dared 11-5-99 passed by the Special Tribunal No. 1 Satkhira in the said Special Tribunal Case and obtained the same on 23-6-99. The petitioner No.1 is the tadbirker of the case and had come to Dhaka on 30-6-99 for consultation with his learned Advocate Mr Nitai Roy Chowdhury and after consultation he went home for managing costs for preferring his case against the impugned order but as ill luck would have it, the petitioner No.1 suddenly fell ill being attacked with Jaundice and under the advice of a doctor had to remain bed ridden up to 20-7-99. The petitioner No.2 was away from home and, as such, none of the petitioners could come to Dhaka to contact with their learned Advocate for preferring appeal and by this time the statutory period of 30 days for preferring appeal expired. Under the above circumstances the petitioners filed the instant writ petition arid obtained the present Rule.

3. No affidavit-in-opposition has been filed by the contesting respondents.

4. Mr Nitai Roy Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the Special Tribunal acted without jurisdiction in passing the impugned order giving direction to return the seized goods to all the 6 accused persons as mentioned in the First Information Report and in the seizure list inasmuch as he did not at all consider the fact disclosed in the final report submitted by the police to the effect that the petitioners are the owners of the seized goods and they are entitled to get back the same and that the other accused persons never challenged the said fact mentioned in the final report and the recommendation made by the Investigating Officer. Learned Advocate further submits that in the Judgment passed by. this Court in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3231of 1997 filed by other accused persons there being no observation or direction to return the seized goods to them, the Special Tribunal acted without jurisdiction in passing the impugned order maintaining the order dated 3-3- 99 which was passed to return the seized goods to all the accused persons giving reference to the Judgment passed in the said Criminal Miscellaneous case and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

5. Mr Oziullah, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 4-7, on the other hand, submits that the Special Tribunal on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case as disclosed in the first information report, seizure list as well as the final report came to the definite finding that the goods were seized from all the 6(six) persons and all of them are entitled to get back the goods which are purely questions of fact and this court in exercising the jurisdiction of judicial review cannot interfere with the said finding of fact unless it can be shown that the tribunal acted without jurisdiction or acted in excess of its jurisdiction. He further submits that in the instant case the tribunal having passed the impugned order with jurisdiction and on consideration of the materials on record there is no scope to interfere with the same by this court. Mr Oziullah lastly submits that the petitioners had an alternative remedy by way of filing an appeal under section 30 of the Special Powers Act and they having not availed the same writ petition itself is not maintainable in law.

6. From the impugned order it appears that the same was passed on an application filed by the present petitioners for reviewing the order dated 6-5-99 passed by the Tribunal whereby the earlier order dated 3-3-99 directing the customs authorities to return the seized goods to the claimants as per their individual statements after realising necesssry VAT as per law on an application filed by 4(four) other accused persons (respondents Nos.4-7 in this writ petition) for returning the seized sarees to them on the finding that the said accused petitioners are entitled to get back their goods as per their individual statement of claim was maintained. From the certified copy of the order sheets of the Special Tribunal No.1, Khulna, it also appears that after the order dated 3-3-99 was passed the present petitioners filed an application praying for staying the operation of the order dated 3-3-99 till the ascertainment of the 'actual owner of the seized goods .and on such' application on 16-3-99 the Tribunal passed the following order;

“--------------- দরখাস্তকারী  বিজ্ঞ এ্যাডভোকেট এবং বিজ্ঞ পি,পির বক্তব্য শুনলাম। তাদের বক্তব্য শ���নে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, ৩-৩-৯৯ তারিখের ৩৭ নং আদেশ এবং এতদসংক্রান্ত পূর্ববর্তী আদেশ সমূহ শূল্ক কর্তৃপক্ষ নিরপেক্ষতার সাথে যথাযথভাবে পালন করছেনা। এমতাবস্থায়, দাবীদারদের প্রতি প্রাপ্য মালামাল হস্তান্তরের পূর্বে তা কি ভাবে কোন দাবীদারকে কি মালামাল হস্তান্তরের পূর্বে তা কি ভাবে কোন দাবীদারদের কি মালামাল হস্তান্তর করা হচ্ছে সেটা অত্র আদালতের পর্যবেক্ষণ করা প্রয়োজন। সেহেতু শুল্ক কর্তৃপক্ষকে দাবীদারের প্রতি দাবীকৃত মালামাল হস্তান্তরের তালিকা অত্র আদালতে দাখিল করে অনুমোদন নেওয়ার জন্য নির্দেশ দেওয়া গেল। অত্রাদালতের অনুমোদন প্রাপ্তির পরই দাবীদারদের প্রতি প্রাপ্য মালামাল শুল্ক কর্তৃপক্ষ হস্তান্তর করতে পারবে। আগামী ৫ (পাঁচ) দিনের মধ্যে শুল্ক কর্তৃপক্ষকে অত্র নির্দেশ মোতাবেক তালিকা সমূহ অত্রাদালতে দাখিল করার নির্দেশ দেওয়া হলো।”

এই আদেশের অনুলুপি অবিলম্বে শুল্ক কর্তৃপক্ষ, সাতক্ষীরার কাছে প্রেরণ করা হোক।”

7. After the passing of the said order, the present petitioners filed another application praying for giving them the seized goods in the light of the facts disclosed in the final report and the said application was fixed for hearing on 20-4-99 after giving notice to the State. In the meantime Superintendent of Customs, Excise and VAT Circle, Satkhira submitted the list of the claimants of the seized goods as has been noted in the order dated 22-3-99 passed by the Tribunal which was kept with the record to be put up on the date fixed. Then on the date fixed, that is on 20-4-99, the presiding Judge being on leave and the Judge-in-charge being engaged with the hearing of other cases, next date was fixed on 6-5-99. The tribunal by his order dated 6-5-99 maintained the order dated 3-3-99 as has already been mentioned hereinabove. On perusal of the impugned order, it appears that the special tribunal passed the same after hearing the parties and considering the allegations made in the First Information Report and the seizure list which is as under;

"Perused the records including FIR, seizure list, FRT and order of High Court carefully. It is evident from the seizure list that those goods were seized from all the 6 persons and all of them are entitled to get back the goods.

The order No.37 dated 3-3-99 of this court is very much clear. We are of the opinion that the goods to be returned to all the 6 FIR named persons as well as seizure list persons. But the customs authority will return the goods on strict scrutiny of the individual claims as well as other evidences on record. Send a copy of this order to the customs authority for compliance.

From the above, it is clear that the tribunal on consideration of the materials before it namely, the 1st Information Report, the seizure list and the Final Report arrived at a finding of fact that the goods Were seized from all the 6 persons and all of them are entitled to get back the goods .

<u>8. The tribunal also gave direction to the customs authority to return the goods on strict scrutiny of the individual claims as well as other evidence on the record. This court exercising the Jurisdiction of judicial review can not sit over the finding of the tribunal as a court of appeal and consequently can not interfere with the said finding of fact which is based on the materials on record. However, we have ourselves also perused the First Information Report where it has been clearly alleged that the goods were seized from all the accused persons and the seizure list was prepared accordingly. In view of the fact that the tribunal has directed the customs authority to return the goods on strict scrutiny of the individual claims as well as other evidence on record, the petitioners will have enough scope to prove their ownership in respect of the seized goods and if they can succeed that the goods were seized from their possession only, in that case they would get back the goods and, as such, we do not see any reason for the petitioners to be aggrieved by the impugned order passed by the tribunal. The basis of the petitioners claim that the goods were seized from their possession only as it appears from the writ petition is the so-called recommendation of the Investigation Officer to the effect that the goods may be released in favour of Aminul Islam and Serajul Islam (petitioners) after realising customs duty and VAT as per Baggage Rules. On scrutiny of the Final Report it appeared to us that the Investigation Officer in a vague way made the said recommendation without specifying with reference to the documents out of 100 seized items of goods, how many items were brought by them and furthermore, in law the Investigating Officer had no legal authority to make any such recommendation and, as such, the petitioners can not claim to get back the goods on such recommendation. In view of the discussion made above, we are of the view that the Special Tribunal No.1 Satkhira passed the impugned order legally and with jurisdiction and we do not find any substance in the submissions made by Mr Nitai Roy Chowdhury.</u>

<u>9. Now, let us see whether the writ petition is maintainable or not. It appears that the impugned order was passed at the instance of the petitioners and in their presence. The order was passed by the Special Tribunal and under section 30 of the Special Powers Act an appeal lies to this court to be filed within 30 days but the petitioners did not file the appeal, instead moved this court in its writ jurisdiction. In paragraph 14 of the writ petition the petitioners have tried to explain the reasons for not preferring the statutory appeal but our considered view is that the explanations are not at all cogent and reasonable and those cannot be accepted to avoid the availability of the alternative remedy. In the case of Nesar Ahmed also known as Babul vs Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali reported in 49 DLR (AD) 1111, it has been held:</u>

<u>"10. But the presence of an alternative remedy does not debar the exercise of jurisdiction by the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution when the facts ,and circumstances of a particular case are such that the accused person had no reasonable opportunity to avail of the statutory remedy under section 30 of the Special Powers Act. whether or not the accused person had such a reasonable opportunity is a question of fact to be decided in each case upon case records and, no hard and fast formula can be laid down to settle the criteria in advance."</u>

<u>In the instant case we have seen that the impugned order was passed at the instance of the petitioners and in their presence and, as such, they had full opportunity to avail of the statutory remedy by way of filing an appeal to this court under section 30 of the Special Powers Act and, as such, we are of the view that the writ petition is also not maintainable in law, and the Rule is liable to be discharged on that count also.</u>

In the result, this Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

End.
